{"selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D03","D05","D06","D07","D08","D09","D10","D11","D12","D13","D15","D16","D17","D18"],"excluded_sources":[{"source_id":"D04","reason":"review_or_nonprimary"},{"source_id":"D14","reason":"task_irrelevant"},{"source_id":"D19","reason":"task_irrelevant"},{"source_id":"D20","reason":"task_irrelevant"}],"selection_rationale":"I retained all documents that report primary experimental, pilot, field, or modeling work on PFAS foam fractionation where operating conditions, water chemistry, and/or PFAS-specific properties are systematically varied or clearly specified, and where distinct performance metrics (removal, enrichment, volume reduction, recovery, mass balance) are quantified.

D01, D02, D03, D05, D06, D07, D08, D09, D10, D11, D12, D13, D15, D16, D17, and D18 are all primary studies focused on foam fractionation or foam-based separation of PFAS (bench, pilot, field, or life-cycle modeling). Across them, they cover a wide range of PFAS structures (long-/short-chain, PFCAs, PFSAs), co-surfactants and organics, salts and cations, and real matrices (groundwater, leachate, municipal wastewater, NF retentate). They also explore key operating variables (air/gas flow, bubble generation method and bubble size, contact time, foam fraction/collection strategy, reactor configuration including semi-batch, continuous, multi-stage, and integrated systems). Many explicitly report and distinguish removal, enrichment factors, recovery, volume reduction, and mass balance closure.

I excluded:
- D04 as it is a review of membrane technologies with only high-level commentary on foam fractionation and no independent primary foam-fractionation experiments or modeling.
- D14 because it is primarily an electrochemical oxidation study in which foam fractionation is only an upstream pre-concentration step; operating or chemistry effects on foam fractionation itself are not explored in a way that provides decision-relevant FF performance data.
- D19 (adsorption onto GAC/PAC/colloidal carbon) and D20 (plasma degradation of PFOA) because they do not use foam fractionation and therefore do not inform the specified task on operating and matrix controls for aqueous PFAS foam fractionation.

The retained set comfortably exceeds the minimum-evidence gate and collectively supports detailed analysis of how PFAS properties, water chemistry, and reactor operation control foam-fractionation performance while keeping performance metrics conceptually distinct.","component_coverage":[{"component_id":"RT06-C1","selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D03","D05","D06","D07","D08","D09","D10","D11","D12","D13","D16","D17","D18"],"rationale":"C1 requires evaluating effects of PFAS structure and water chemistry. Multiple selected studies explicitly address these:
- PFAS chain length and functional group: D01, D05, D06, D08, D09, D10, D11, D12, D16, D18 examine long- vs short-chain PFCAs and PFSAs, including differences between sulfonates and carboxylates and species-specific removal behaviors in real matrices.
- Co-surfactants / foam agents: D01 (thickener, Fe(III)), D02 (systematic comparison of anionic/cationic/zwitterionic/nonionic cosurfactants), D06 (CTAB co-foaming agent), D07 (OTCS as modified biopolymer), D10 (SDS addition), D15 (14C-PFOA with controlled surfactant system), D18 (cosurfactant dosing on NF concentrate).
- Organic matter and microbial solids: D01 (NOM), D03 (wastewater and sludge with endogenous surfactants), D05 (organic complexes in leachate), D07 (natural organic matter/suspended particulates noted), D11/D12 (field groundwater with natural DOC), D13 (explicitly links microbial communities and foam formation/enrichment).
- Salts and competing constituents: D01 (ionic strength, CaCl2/NaNO3), D09 (dissolved solids and ozone chemistry), D10 (systematic variation of Na+, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+), D17 (ionic strength and matrix effects from leachate context), plus inherent salinity/complex matrices in D05, D08, D09, D11, D12, D16, D18.
Together these allow assessment of how PFAS properties and water chemistry co-control FF performance, without over-generalizing beyond the tested structures and matrices."},{"component_id":"RT06-C2","selected_source_ids":["D01","D02","D03","D05","D06","D07","D08","D09","D10","D11","D12","D13","D15","D16","D17","D18"],"rationale":"C2 focuses on gas/air flow, bubble size, residence time, recycle, foam collection, and reactor configuration. Many selected studies directly manipulate or characterize these:
- Gas flow and residence/contact time: D01 (varying air flow rate, multi-stage vs single-stage), D03 (two airflow phases, batch mode), D06 (air flow and CTAB dosing, semi-batch), D08 (air flowrate and water height effects), D09 (air/ozone flowrate optimization), D10 (air flow coupled to venturi recirculation, modeling of hydrodynamic effects), D15 (comparison of flow regimes and gas flow rates), D16 (systematic variation of air flow Q_air and contact time t_c), D17 (foam fraction and contact time as design variables), D18 (batch vs continuous mode and contact time).
- Bubble size and generation: D06 (foam and bubble characterization), D07 (micro-nano bubbles and bubble size distribution), D08 (discussion of bubble size and surface area), D09 (different spargers), D10 (quantified bubble size distributions and Sauter mean radius), D11/D12 (design geometry and bubble production methods for SAFF), D15 (discussion of bubbly flow vs larger bubbles), D16 (notes potential for alternative bubble introduction such as electrochemical bubbles).
- Foam collection strategy and foam fraction: D01 (single- vs multi-stage, staged operation), D02 (steady-state column with continuous foam extraction), D03 (overflow/suction collection of foam), D06 (vacuum-controlled foam removal), D07 (vacuum pump extraction, foam collapse), D08 (batch foam harvesting and enrichment), D09 (semi-continuous overflow with differing foam wetness), D15 (tank experiments with defined foam collection), D16 (systematic variation of foam fraction %foam and its effect on concentration), D17 (one- vs three-stage FF with different foam fractions), D18 (foam-to-water ratio FWR for batch vs continuous runs).
- Reactor configuration, recycle, and staging: D02 (continuous column with modeling), D03 (column operation on real wastewater and MBR influent), D05 (membrane electrochemical reactor integrating foam generation and volume reduction), D06 (semi-batch FF with co-foaming agent), D07 (micro-nano bubble enhanced Plexiglas column), D11/D12 (multi-stage SAFF commercial systems, including series configurations), D13 (semi-batch PMMA columns on activated sludge), D16 (pilot-scale continuous FF with controlled influent/effluent split and foam fraction), D17 (LCA/LCC comparing one- vs three-stage FF systems), D18 (NF concentrate FF in both batch and continuous arrangements).
These collectively support comparative analysis of how reactor operation and configuration influence foam fractionation performance under specified conditions, while retaining the context of PFAS structure and matrix to respect the task boundaries."},{"component_id":"RT06-C3","selected_source_ids":["D01","D03","D06","D07","D08","D09","D10","D12","D13","D15","D16","D17","D18"],"rationale":"C3 requires explicit treatment of removal, recovery, enrichment, mass balance, and volume reduction as distinct performance measures. Several selected studies define and use these metrics separately:
- Removal vs enrichment vs recovery: D01 defines and reports PFAS removal, enrichment factor (single and multi-stage), and mass balance; D06 explicitly defines volume reduction factor (VRF), enrichment factor (EF), and mass recovery, and discusses why high removal without adequate VRF/enrichment may be misleading; D08 calculates foamate enrichment factors, PFAS recovery, and removal separately; D12 discusses the trade-off between high removal (recovery) and high enrichment in foamate/concentrate, including multi-stage operation.
- Volume reduction / foam fraction: D01 (multi-stage removal per stage and cumulative), D05 (reports large reduction in leachate volume due to entrainment in foam), D06 (VRF and its optimization), D07 (foam water content and foam volume under different conditions), D08 (foamate volume vs enrichment), D09 (foamate wetness and volume for air vs ozone FF), D16 (systematic analysis of foam fraction %foam and resulting foam concentrations), D17 (explicitly links lower foam fraction to decreased hazardous waste volume and environmental burdens, while recognizing possible loss of treatment efficacy), D18 (foam-to-water ratio and foamate recovery in batch vs continuous trials).
- Mass balance closure and partitioning: D01 reports satisfactory mass balances for many samples; D03 and D13 partition PFAS between bulk liquid, foam liquid, and solids, with D13 calculating enrichment factors in both liquid and solid foam phases; D06 and D08 compare total mass removed from bulk with mass found in foamate; D15 uses 14C-PFOA to track total mass through FF and subsequent electrochemical oxidation, reducing ambiguity in mass balance.
Across these studies, the metrics are defined and reported distinctly rather than being conflated, enabling a review that respects the required distinction between removal, recovery, enrichment, mass-balance closure, and volume reduction."}]}

You are selecting primary PFAS treatment studies for a focused professional
review. You receive one task and an anonymized, BGE-ranked list of candidate
document cards.

Classify every candidate card. Select every document that is an independent
primary study, is directly relevant to at least one task component, and
contains extractable decision-relevant evidence. There is no target number of
selected documents and no penalty for retaining all eligible studies.

Eligible evidence includes:

- primary experiments, pilot or field deployments, and quantitative modeling
  or life-cycle studies;
- complementary matrices, PFAS scopes, operating regimes, endpoints, and
  scales;
- documents with concrete methods, conditions, results, limitations, residuals,
  energy, or cost evidence; and
- evidence that permits meaningful comparison or explains non-comparability.

Do not select a document merely because its title repeats task words. Do not
select reviews, perspectives, reference lists, duplicate records, or the
held-out defining review. Do not exclude an otherwise eligible study merely
because another selected study reports similar findings. Do not infer facts
absent from a card. Selection is document-level only: do not write the review
and do not score candidate answers.

Every candidate source_id must appear exactly once, either in
selected_source_ids or excluded_sources. Each required component must be
covered by at least one selected source. Return selected_source_ids in BGE rank
order.

Return one JSON object following the supplied schema exactly.

Review task:
{"review_brief":"Prepare a focused review of how PFAS properties, water chemistry, and reactor operation control foam-fractionation performance.","task_id":"RT06","title":"Identifying the operating conditions that control PFAS foam fractionation"}

[{"component_id":"RT06-C1","requirement":"Evaluate effects of PFAS chain length and functional group, co-surfactants, organic matter, salts, and competing constituents."},{"component_id":"RT06-C2","requirement":"Compare gas flow, bubble size, residence time, recycle, foam collection, and reactor configuration."},{"component_id":"RT06-C3","requirement":"Interpret removal, recovery, enrichment, mass balance, and volume reduction as distinct performance measures."}]

Task boundaries:

least 6 eligible primary sources or report the

component_coverage.rationale:
C1 requires evaluating effects of PFAS structure and water chemistry. Multiple selected studies explicitly address these:
- PFAS chain length and functional group: D01, D05, D06, D08, D09, D10, D11, D12, D16, D18 examine long- vs short-chain PFCAs and PFSAs, including differences between sulfonates and carboxylates and species-specific removal behaviors in real matrices.
- Co-surfactants / foam agents: D01 (thickener, Fe(III)), D02 (systematic comparison of anionic/cationic/zwitterionic/nonionic cosurfactants), D06 (CTAB co-foaming agent), D07 (OTCS as modified biopolymer), D10 (SDS addition), D15 (14C-PFOA with controlled surfactant system), D18 (cosurfactant dosing on NF concentrate).
- Organic matter and microbial solids: D01 (NOM), D03 (wastewater and sludge with endogenous surfactants), D05 (organic complexes in leachate), D07 (natural organic matter/suspended particulates noted), D11/D12 (field groundwater with natural DOC), D13 (explicitly links microbial communities and foam formation/enrichment).
- Salts and competing constituents: D01 (ionic strength, CaCl2/NaNO3), D09 (dissolved solids and ozone chemistry), D10 (systematic variation of Na+, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+), D17 (ionic strength and matrix effects from leachate context), plus inherent salinity/complex matrices in D05, D08, D09, D11, D12, D16, D18.
Together these allow assessment of how PFAS properties and water chemistry co-control FF performance, without over-generalizing beyond the tested structures and matrices.

C2 focuses on gas/air flow, bubble size, residence time, recycle, foam collection, and reactor configuration. Many selected studies directly manipulate or characterize these:
- Gas flow and residence/contact time: D01 (varying air flow rate, multi-stage vs single-stage), D03 (two airflow phases, batch mode), D06 (air flow and CTAB dosing, semi-batch), D08 (air flowrate and water height effects), D09 (air/ozone flowrate optimization), D10 (air flow coupled to venturi recirculation, modeling of hydrodynamic effects), D15 (comparison of flow regimes and gas flow rates), D16 (systematic variation of air flow Q_air and contact time t_c), D17 (foam fraction and contact time as design variables), D18 (batch vs continuous mode and contact time).
- Bubble size and generation: D06 (foam and bubble characterization), D07 (micro-nano bubbles and bubble size distribution), D08 (discussion of bubble size and surface area), D09 (different spargers), D10 (quantified bubble size distributions and Sauter mean radius), D11/D12 (design geometry and bubble production methods for SAFF), D15 (discussion of bubbly flow vs larger bubbles), D16 (notes potential for alternative bubble introduction such as electrochemical bubbles).
- Foam collection strategy and foam fraction: D01 (single- vs multi-stage, staged operation), D02 (steady-state column with continuous foam extraction), D03 (overflow/suction collection of foam), D06 (vacuum-controlled foam removal), D07 (vacuum pump extraction, foam collapse), D08 (batch foam harvesting and enrichment), D09 (semi-continuous overflow with differing foam wetness), D15 (tank experiments with defined foam collection), D16 (systematic variation of foam fraction %foam and its effect on concentration), D17 (one- vs three-stage FF with different foam fractions), D18 (foam-to-water ratio FWR for batch vs continuous runs).
- Reactor configuration, recycle, and staging: D02 (continuous column with modeling), D03 (column operation on real wastewater and MBR influent), D05 (membrane electrochemical reactor integrating foam generation and volume reduction), D06 (semi-batch FF with co-foaming agent), D07 (micro-nano bubble enhanced Plexiglas column), D11/D12 (multi-stage SAFF commercial systems, including series configurations), D13 (semi-batch PMMA columns on activated sludge), D16 (pilot-scale continuous FF with controlled influent/effluent split and foam fraction), D17 (LCA/LCC comparing one- vs three-stage FF systems), D18 (NF concentrate FF in both batch and continuous arrangements).
These collectively support comparative analysis of how reactor operation and configuration influence foam fractionation performance under specified conditions, while retaining the context of PFAS structure and matrix to respect the task boundaries.

C3 requires explicit treatment of removal, recovery, enrichment, mass balance, and volume reduction as distinct performance measures. Several selected studies define and use these metrics separately:
- Removal vs enrichment vs recovery: D01 defines and reports PFAS removal, enrichment factor (single and multi-stage), and mass balance; D06 explicitly defines volume reduction factor (VRF), enrichment factor (EF), and mass recovery, and discusses why high removal without adequate VRF/enrichment may be misleading; D08 calculates foamate enrichment factors, PFAS recovery, and removal separately; D12 discusses the trade-off between high removal (recovery) and high enrichment in foamate/concentrate, including multi-stage operation.
- Volume reduction / foam fraction: D01 (multi-stage removal per stage and cumulative), D05 (reports large reduction in leachate volume due to entrainment in foam), D06 (VRF and its optimization), D07 (foam water content and foam volume under different conditions), D08 (foamate volume vs enrichment), D09 (foamate wetness and volume for air vs ozone FF), D16 (systematic analysis of foam fraction %foam and resulting foam concentrations), D17 (explicitly links lower foam fraction to decreased hazardous waste volume and environmental burdens, while recognizing possible loss of treatment efficacy), D18 (foam-to-water ratio and foamate recovery in batch vs continuous trials).
- Mass balance closure and partitioning: D01 reports satisfactory mass balances for many samples; D03 and D13 partition PFAS between bulk liquid, foam liquid, and solids, with D13 calculating enrichment factors in both liquid and solid foam phases; D06 and D08 compare total mass removed from bulk with mass found in foamate; D15 uses 14C-PFOA to track total mass through FF and subsequent electrochemical oxidation, reducing ambiguity in mass balance.
Across these studies, the metrics are defined and reported distinctly rather than being conflated, enabling a review that respects the required distinction between removal, recovery, enrichment, mass-balance closure, and volume reduction.

result.selection_rationale:
I retained all documents that report primary experimental, pilot, field, or modeling work on PFAS foam fractionation where operating conditions, water chemistry, and/or PFAS-specific properties are systematically varied or clearly specified, and where distinct performance metrics (removal, enrichment, volume reduction, recovery, mass balance) are quantified.

D01, D02, D03, D05, D06, D07, D08, D09, D10, D11, D12, D13, D15, D16, D17, and D18 are all primary studies focused on foam fractionation or foam-based separation of PFAS (bench, pilot, field, or life-cycle modeling). Across them, they cover a wide range of PFAS structures (long-/short-chain, PFCAs, PFSAs), co-surfactants and organics, salts and cations, and real matrices (groundwater, leachate, municipal wastewater, NF retentate). They also explore key operating variables (air/gas flow, bubble generation method and bubble size, contact time, foam fraction/collection strategy, reactor configuration including semi-batch, continuous, multi-stage, and integrated systems). Many explicitly report and distinguish removal, enrichment factors, recovery, volume reduction, and mass balance closure.

I excluded:
- D04 as it is a review of membrane technologies with only high-level commentary on foam fractionation and no independent primary foam-fractionation experiments or modeling.
- D14 because it is primarily an electrochemical oxidation study in which foam fractionation is only an upstream pre-concentration step; operating or chemistry effects on foam fractionation itself are not explored in a way that provides decision-relevant FF performance data.
- D19 (adsorption onto GAC/PAC/colloidal carbon) and D20 (plasma degradation of PFOA) because they do not use foam fractionation and therefore do not inform the specified task on operating and matrix controls for aqueous PFAS foam fractionation.

The retained set comfortably exceeds the minimum-evidence gate and collectively supports detailed analysis of how PFAS properties, water chemistry, and reactor operation control foam-fractionation performance while keeping performance metrics conceptually distinct.
